question_text: According to the course material, man plays a unique role in resource development: he acts both as a resource as well as a:
explanation: Man is both a resource and a resource-creating factor.

question_text: According to the course material, as a resource, man is an inexhaustible store of energy and skill; in the preindustrial era, man served more as a resource than resource creating factor because human labour was an important factor in the:
explanation: Preindustrial man was mainly labour in the production process.

question_text: According to the course material, nature provides most of its endowments in the form of 'neutral stuff'; it is man who by his ingenuity, skill and initiative turns this neutral stuff into:
explanation: Man turns neutral stuff into resources.

question_text: According to the course material, knowledge is truly the mother of all resources; with the help of knowledge, man finds new resources and makes old ones more useful; coal is no longer the only source of inanimate energy, which is now also derived from petroleum, gas and:
explanation: Inanimate energy also comes from petroleum, gas and waterpower.

question_text: According to the course material, man is both the most dynamic agent of production and the beneficiary of the entire process of resource development; to perform this role properly, man must be physically fit and healthy and must be properly:
explanation: Man must be fit, educated and trained.

question_text: According to the course material, plastic pollution involves the accumulation of plastic products in the environment that adversely affects human habitat; plastics pollution is categorized into micro, meso or macro debris, based on the:
explanation: Plastic debris is categorized by size: micro, meso or macro.

question_text: According to the course material, plastic pollution has negative effect on land, waterways and oceans; living organisms, particularly marine animals, are also affected; humans are also affected, such as through the disruption of the thyroid hormone axis or:
explanation: Humans may suffer thyroid/hormone disruption from plastics.

question_text: According to the course material, the distribution of plastic debris is influenced by wind and ocean currents, coastline geography, urban areas, and trade routes; human population is another critical factor; plastics are more likely to be found in enclosed regions such as the Caribbean and:
explanation: Enclosed regions such as the Caribbean and West Africa/Nigeria accumulate plastics.

question_text: According to the course material, plastics can also be used as vectors for chemical contaminants such as persistent organic pollutants and:
explanation: Plastics can vector POPs and heavy metals.

question_text: According to the course material, textile waste is a material that is deemed unusable for its original purpose by the owner; it can include fashion and textile industry waste created during production, and consumer waste created during:
explanation: Textile waste includes industry waste and consumer use/disposal waste.

question_text: According to the course material, pre-consumer textile waste is waste generated in the fashion supply chain before the textile reached the consumer; examples include textile swatch waste, cut-and-sew scraps, end-of-roll waste, sampling yardage waste, damaged textile waste, finished clothing waste and:
explanation: Pre-consumer waste includes samples, scraps, end-of-roll and unsold finished clothing.

question_text: According to the course material, post-consumer textile waste is waste generated and collected after the consumer has used and disposed of it; secondhand clothing waste is popularly called okrika or tokunbo in:
explanation: Secondhand clothing is called okrika or tokunbo in Nigeria.

question_text: According to the course material, a chemical hazard is a type of occupational hazard caused by exposure to chemicals in the workplace; exposure can cause acute or long-term detrimental health effects; types include neurotoxins, immune agents, dermatologic agents, carcinogens, reproductive toxins, systemic toxins, asthmagens, pneumoconiotic agents and:
explanation: Hazardous chemicals include neurotoxins, carcinogens, sensitizers and others listed.

question_text: According to the course material, long-term exposure to chemicals such as silica dust, engine exhausts, tobacco smoke, and/or lead have been shown to increase risk of heart disease, stroke, and:
explanation: Long-term exposure increases heart disease, stroke and high blood pressure risk.

question_text: According to the course material, types of chemical hazards include liquids such as acids and solvents especially if they do not have a label, vapors and fumes, and:
explanation: Types: unlabeled liquids, vapors/fumes, flammable materials.

question_text: According to the course material, routes of exposure of chemical hazards include ingestion, inhalation from fumes, poisoning and:
explanation: Routes: ingestion, inhalation, poisoning, explosion.

question_text: According to the course material, hazard pictographs are distinctive as they are shaped like a diamond with red borders; examples include Explosive (exploding bomb), Flammable (flame), Oxidizing (flame above a circle), Corrosive, Acute Toxicity (skull and crossbones), and Hazardous to environment:
explanation: Environment hazard pictograph is a dead tree and fish.

question_text: According to the course material, in chemical first aid the majority of sources recommend that it is best to rinse any contacted skin or eye with water for at least:
explanation: Rinse contacted skin or eye with water for at least 15-20 minutes.

question_text: According to the course material, recommended flush time for strong alkalis such as sodium, potassium or calcium hydroxide is:
explanation: Strong alkalis: flush 60 minutes.

question_text: According to the course material, Science and Technology Studies is an interdisciplinary field that examines how science and technology shape societies, cultures, and the environment and how social, cultural, and environmental factors shape the:
explanation: STS examines two-way shaping of science/technology and society.

question_text: According to the course material, science investigates the physical world, including human beings and the material they are made of; technology entails making materials used by society, and in the production and dissemination of science; society embraces the sum total of our interactions as:
explanation: Society is the sum of human interactions.

question_text: According to the course material, when we study science and technology we can take an internal or an external perspective; an internal perspective starts with the principles and assumptions that scientists and engineers themselves work with; we usually rely on experts for an:
explanation: An internal perspective usually relies on experts.

question_text: According to the course material, a critical stance is the deliberate creation of distance between us and the object we study; in order to be critical we must step back and ask:
explanation: A critical stance requires stepping back to ask broad questions.

question_text: According to the course material, gas state chemicals will be inhaled or liquid state chemicals can be absorbed by the:
explanation: Physical state determines route: gas inhaled, liquid absorbed by skin.

question_text: According to the course material, environment means surrounding external conditions influencing development or growth of people, animal or plants; environmental effects include climate change, environmental degradation, pollution, resource depletion, toxicants and:
explanation: Environmental effects include climate change, pollution, wastes and related issues.

question_text: According to the course material, in the preindustrial era many regions remained economically backward on account of scarcity of population; in this respect, man was no better than an animal because he had only natural wants and natural capacities and therefore commanded only:
explanation: Preindustrial man commanded only natural resources.

question_text: According to the course material, recommended flush time for non to mild irritants is 5 minutes; for moderate to severe irritants and chemicals that cause acute toxicity it is 15-20 minutes; for most corrosives it is:
explanation: Most corrosives: flush 30 minutes.

question_text: According to the course material, a 2017 SBU report found evidence that workplace exposure to silica dust, engine exhaust or welding fumes is associated with:
explanation: SBU 2017: silica dust, engine exhaust or welding fumes associated with heart disease.

question_text: According to the course material, technology is a broad concept that deals with a species' usage and knowledge of tools and crafts, and how it affects a species' ability to control and adapt to its:
explanation: Technology affects ability to control and adapt to the environment.

question_text: According to the course material, from the beginning of time man has strived to improve his way and quality of life; the totality of the use and application of his knowledge, skills, tools, and materials constitutes what we today describe as:
explanation: Knowledge, skills, tools and materials together constitute technology.

question_text: According to the course material, developed nations of the world like America, Germany, France etc. boast of several scientific inventions; science and technology is the pivot of any nation's development; a nation without science and technology is definitely a:
explanation: Without science and technology a nation is backward/undeveloped.

question_text: According to the course material, these groupings of science are empirical sciences, which mean the knowledge must be based on observable phenomena and capable of being tested for its validity by other researchers working under the:
explanation: Empirical science must be observable and testable under the same conditions.
